approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change how rural research and development levies are set by removing fixed maximum rates from the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act 1999.
Future levy rate changes would be made through regulations alone, without amending the Act, and regulations could not set a rate above what the relevant industry body recommends.
The bill also makes technical amendments to remove obsolete provisions and improve consistency between schedules.
Removes product-specific maximum levy rates for research and development and marketing levies from the Act's schedules.
Specifies that regulations cannot set a levy rate higher than the rate recommended by the industry body.
Includes technical amendments to remove provisions no longer needed and improve schedule consistency.
Primary producers, rural research and development corporations, and industry bodies that pay or manage levies.

Moved the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment Bill 2013, a companion bill removing the legislated maximum rate for charges on agricultural commodities imported or exported, requiring new rates to be recommended by industry in consultation with charge payers.

Referred the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013, the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment Bill 2013 and the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Amendment Bill 2013 to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 and companion levy bills amending 10 acts, noting they were first introduced on 19 June before lapsing when the election was called, and welcomed extending marketing activities and matched funding to statutory research and development corporations.

Argued that the bill builds on the research and development corporation model established in 1989 under the Hawke government, and that it lets statutory bodies undertake marketing, extends government matching of voluntary contributions, removes the requirement to submit annual operating plans for ministerial approval, and allows individual fishery sectors to set their own levies.

Supported the bill's marketing provisions for statutory research and development corporations, but argued that the Coles and Woolworths duopoly discourages food innovation by quickly copying successful branded products as cheaper home-brand versions, citing Heinz's departure from regional Victoria as a result.

Supported the rural research and development bills, noting a similar bill was introduced on 19 June in the 43rd Parliament but lapsed when parliament was prorogued in August, and welcomed provisions letting statutory bodies market their industries and matching voluntary research contributions without changing existing levy rates.

Supported the bill's marketing provisions, noting that only 22 per cent of prawns sold in New South Wales are caught locally, and that the electorate's macadamia growers invest more than $4 million a year in research and development to keep pace with export demand.

Welcomed extending industry-specific levies to fisheries under the National Food Plan, and warned that Australia's spending on rural research and development has fallen from ninth to 16th internationally since 2000, threatening future farm productivity growth.

Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013 and related bills, describing how Grains Research and Development Corporation levies of about $2.50 per tonne generate roughly $80 million a year, to be matched at an increased rate of $1.25 for every industry dollar under the coalition's election commitment.

Moved to schedule non-controversial government bills for consideration from 12:45 pm, including amendments to the Australian Civilian Corps, Import Processing Charges, Grape and Wine Authority, Offshore Petroleum, Rural Research and Development, and Customs Anti-Dumping Commission. Also moved to set general business order for the day, prioritising Senator Moore's motion on pre-election commitments and government document orders.
